jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Mackinac Island is one of Michigan's most iconic destinations — a community where horse-drawn carriages and bicycles are the only transportation and Victorian architecture meets the pristine waters of Lake Huron. The Mackinac Island Convention & Visitors Bureau (MICVB) promotes the island to visitors, advances the tourism industry through state and federal advocacy, and serves the local business community through the Mackinac Island Tourism Bureau.

The MICVB operates with four full-time and four seasonal staff, and manages relationships with a state lobbying firm, federal lobbying firm, PR firm, and digital advertising agency. The ED also oversees the MITB-PAC — a federal Political Action Committee advocating for H-2B Visa reform — and represents the island on statewide travel and tourism boards.

THE OPPORTUNITY:
The MICVB Board of Directors seeks an exceptional leader to serve as its next Executive Director. This is a rare opportunity to lead a high-profile destination organization on one of America's most storied islands — stewarding a beloved brand, championing the island's interests in Lansing and Washington, D.C., and serving the vibrant business community that makes Mackinac Island extraordinary.
The next ED will inherit a strong organizational foundation, established advocacy relationships, and deep community goodwill — with the opportunity to shape the bureau's next chapter, deepen member engagement, and ensure Mackinac Island remains a world-class destination for generations to come.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Organizational Leadership
Serve as chief executive of the MICVB, Mackinac Island Tourism Bureau, and MITB-PAC
Lead and develop a team of four full-time and four seasonal staff
Report to the Board of Directors on performance, strategy, and financial health
Manage contracts with the state and federal lobbying firms, PR firm, and digital advertising agency

Destination Marketing & Brand
Oversee brand strategy and positioning of Mackinac Island as a premier travel destination
Direct advertising, PR, content, and social media programs that drive visitation and overnight stays
Manage visitor information booth operations
Lead event programming that animates the destination and generates media attention

Advocacy & Government Relations
Lead state-level advocacy with the Michigan Legislature and state agencies
Direct federal advocacy through the island's D.C. lobbying firm and MITB-PAC
Represent Mackinac Island on statewide travel and tourism boards and coalitions
Cultivate relationships with elected officials and policy stakeholders at all levels

Mackinac Island Tourism Bureau & Member Engagement
Lead the Mackinac Island Tourism Bureau — the island's chamber of commerce — overseeing member recruitment, retention, and programming
Serve as a trusted resource and advocate for the local business community
Foster collaboration across tourism, retail, hospitality, and civic stakeholders

Finance & Administration
Develop and manage the annual budget across all three entities
Pursue grants, sponsorships, and revenue diversification opportunities
Ensure compliance with all nonprofit, Tourism Bureau, and MITB-PAC regulatory requirements

QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS:
Required
Minimum 5 years of experience in tourism, destination marketing, DMO management, hospitality, or a related field
Proven ability to lead a small professional team, including seasonal staff
Experience overseeing marketing, advertising, PR, or brand programs
Strong relationship-building skills with the ability to represent the organization at government, industry, and community levels
Experience managing vendor or agency relationships (advertising, PR, lobbying, or similar)
Financial management experience including budget development in a nonprofit or association setting
Seasonal island residency required — executive housing on Mackinac Island is provided with a portion of costs subsidized by the employer
Ability to travel as needed for advocacy, conferences, and industry events

Preferred
Experience in government relations or advocacy at the state or federal level
Familiarity with PAC administration, compliance, and H-2B Visa workforce policy
Experience in a seasonal, island, or resort destination market
Existing relationships with Michigan tourism stakeholders and/or elected officials
Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, public administration, or business; graduate degree a plus
Fluency in digital advertising, social media strategy, and content marketing

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS
Salary-Commensurate with experience; competitive with the scope of this role
Health Insurance-Comprehensive health insurance provided
Retirement-401(k) retirement plan
Residency & Housing-Access to executive housing on Mackinac Island with a portion of costs subsidized by the employer
Remote Work-Remote work opportunities available during the off-season
Vacation & Leave-Comprehensive vacation and leave policies
Professional Development-Support for industry conferences and continuing education

HOW TO APPLY:

Submit a letter of interest, current resume, and three professional references to the MICVB Board of Directors. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis; the position is open until filled.

Submit applications to:

MICVB Board of Directors — Executive Director Search

Email: hr@mackinacisland.org

Web: mackinacisland.org

All inquiries are treated with strict confidentiality.

The MICVB is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace.

jobs.description:
Video Testimonial

Job Details

The Baptist Health/UAMS Medical Education Program is seeking a Transitional Year Program Director.

The Transitional Year Program Director provides leadership, administration, and educational oversight for the ACGME-accredited Transitional Year Residency Program.

The Program Director is responsible for the design, implementation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of the residency program; compliance with ACGME Institutional, Common, and Transitional Year Program Requirements; resident recruitment and development; faculty engagement; and achievement of program aims and outcomes. The Program Director fosters a supportive learning environment that prepares residents for advanced specialty training and promotes excellence in patient care, professionalism, well-being, and scholarly activity.

This position serves within the Baptist Health–UAMS Medical Education Program, a partnership between Baptist Health—the largest private health care system in Arkansas—and the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS), the state’s only academic health sciences university. This collaboration combines the academic excellence and research resources of UAMS with Baptist Health’s community-based care model to train compassionate, skilled family physicians who are prepared to meet the evolving health needs of Arkansas and beyond.

Qualifications:

Minimum Qualifications

MD or DO degree from an accredited institution.
Board certification by an ABMS or AOA-approved specialty board in a discipline relevant to the educational program.
Eligibility for and ability to maintain an unrestricted Arkansas medical license.
Minimum of three years of documented educational and/or administrative experience in graduate medical education.
Demonstrated commitment to resident education, mentorship, and academic leadership.
Excellent interpersonal, communication, organizational, and leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior experience as a Residency Program Director, Associate Program Director, or Core Faculty member.
Experience with ACGME accreditation processes, site visits, self-studies, and ADS reporting.
Experience in curriculum design, resident assessment, faculty development, and quality improvement.
Demonstrated success fostering inclusive learning environments and resident well-being initiatives.

Protected Time and Support

The position includes protected administrative time and institutional support commensurate with ACGME requirements and program needs.

Additional Information:

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Provide strategic and operational leadership for all aspects of the Transitional Year Residency Program.
Maintain substantial involvement in resident education and program administration.
Ensure ongoing compliance with ACGME accreditation requirements, policies, and reporting obligations.
Develop, implement, and evaluate curriculum, required rotations, electives, didactics, quality improvement, patient safety, and professional development activities.
Lead resident recruitment, selection, onboarding, mentoring, and career advising activities.
Oversee competency-based assessments, Milestones reporting, semiannual resident review, promotion, remediation, and graduation decisions.
Chair or oversee the Clinical Competency Committee and Program Evaluation Committee.
Conduct Annual Program Evaluation and implement continuous quality improvement initiatives.

Recruit, support, and develop faculty participating in the residency program.
Collaborate with institutional leadership, the DIO, GMEC, participating sites, and specialty departments.
Maintain accurate program records, Accreditation Data System updates, and preparation for accreditation reviews and site visits. Management/Financial

Ensures that the Community is prepared for inspection by regulatory agencies through regular auditing and updating of Community policies and procedures, medical records documentation, monitoring of environmental standards, etc.
Maintains monthly financial reports and provides explanation for variances.

Ensures accounts receivables are collected on a timely basis.
Ensure systems and processes are in place to continuously monitor quality of care, service delivery and regulatory compliance. Review quality indicator outcomes; identify and address variance.
Optimizes all opportunities to generate revenue and ancillary revenue.
Maintains and increases occupancy in accordance with budget.
Actively promotes staff participation and involvement in the day-to-day operations and decision making of the Community.
Promotes team building through participation and/or leadership at regular staff meetings.
Provides ongoing support, direction, supervision, and feedback regarding job performance of all staff.
Communicates with team members to ensure they are fully informed regarding any questions that might be asked by residents and their families, as well as prospective Residents and their families.
Oversee and/ or manage efforts related to recruitment, hiring, employee relations and separations of team members in accordance with administrative policy.
Assures that all staff files are created and maintained properly.
Coordinates evaluation process, reviews all evaluations, and completes evaluations for all department heads.
Manages disciplinary process throughout the Community.
Lead the management team in support of the mission and values of the organization in accordance with community values.

Resident Care

Assures high-quality services as needed and desired by Residents.
Ensures Resident rights are protected.
Ensures staff, Residents, and families are educated about Resident rights.
Works with Wellness Director in coordination of move-in process to ensure leases and
Resident Service Plans are coordinated and properly carried out.
Responds to family, resident, and team member requests in a timely manner.
Acts as liaison between management, Residents, and families.
Maintains competitive market analysis data and maintains a detailed competitor comparative analysis (including rates, unit sizes, services, and amenities).
Ensures use of Vitals within the Community is timely and accurate.
Ensures that the overall Community makes a positive first impression.
Works to resolve any Community presentation issues.
Maintains or grows occupancy to maximum levels.
Works collaboratively with department heads to emphasize the team’s role in sales and participation in the Community Marketing Action Plan and Sales Action Plan.
Assigns Manager on Duty for weekend coverage as scheduled.

Sales/Marketing

Represents the Community in public settings.
Works within the local community promoting the AgeWell Solvere Living Managed Community.
Ensures use of Sherpa within the Community is timely and accurate.
Able to generate leads and helps to close sales.

Compliance And Safety

Enforces OSHA regulations and safety procedures.
Ensures full compliance with all laws and regulations related to the operation of an assisted living facility.
Follows all emergency procedures.
Understands the safety policies and procedures.
Investigates and reviews all on-site injuries.

Qualifications

State required licensing and certification (if applicable).
Excellent customer service and public relations skills.
Experience working with seniors.
Experience in successfully operating and maintaining a customer-focused environment in a senior living facility.
Demonstrates proficiency in Microsoft Office.
Meets all current requirements of state regulations for licensed assisted living communities.
Must have demonstrated integrity, and leadership skills.
Possesses a sincere passion for working with our senior population.
Promotes the community in a positive manner and effectively communicates the company values to residents, families, visitors, and team members.
Physically able to bend and reach.
Physically able to push and pull and lift up to 40-50 pounds if necessary.
Physically able to stand for extended periods of time.
Spends at least 30% of time on travel to referral sources in market area.

jobs.description:
JOB POSTING DETAILS

Job Title

Director of Advancement

Job Type

Full Time

Position Level

Experienced

Job Description

Position Overview

The Director of Advancement is a visionary relationship builder and strategic fundraising leader responsible for advancing the mission and long-term sustainability of St. Andrew's Schools through philanthropy, community engagement, and institutional partnerships.

Working closely with the Head of School, Board of Trustees, and Administrative Leadership Team, the Director develops and executes a comprehensive advancement strategy that inspires generosity, deepens constituent engagement, and secures philanthropic support for the school's strategic priorities. This leader cultivates meaningful relationships with alumni, parents, grandparents, foundations, corporations, community leaders, and friends of the school while fostering a vibrant culture of philanthropy grounded in Queen Emma's legacy of compassion, service, and educational opportunity.

Above all, the Director of Advancement understands that philanthropy is about people, purpose, and relationships. Successful fundraising begins with listening, building trust, and helping donors connect their passions with opportunities to make a meaningful difference in the lives of students.

As St. Andrew's Schools begins an exciting new chapter as a fully coeducational PK–12 independent Episcopal school, the Director of Advancement will play a pivotal role in shaping the school's future by securing the philanthropic resources needed to support transformational initiatives, exceptional educational programs, student scholarships, faculty excellence, and campus improvements. This leader will help ensure that the generosity of today's donors creates life-changing opportunities for tomorrow's students, strengthening the school for generations to come.

The Director of Advancement serves as a member of the Administrative Leadership Team and works collaboratively across the school to strengthen community engagement, celebrate the school's impact, and ensure the long-term vitality of St. Andrew's Schools.

What Success Looks Like

During the first 12–18 months, the Director of Advancement will work collaboratively with the Head of School, Administrative Leadership Team, and Board of Trustees to make meaningful progress in the following areas:

Strengthen Philanthropic Relationships

Build authentic relationships with current and prospective donors, expanding the school's pipeline of individual, corporate, and foundation supporters while increasing donor engagement, stewardship, and long-term investment in the mission of St. Andrew's Schools.

Grow a Culture of Philanthropy

Foster a school-wide culture in which trustees, faculty, staff, alumni, parents, grandparents, and friends understand the transformational impact of philanthropy and actively champion the school's mission and strategic priorities.

Increase Sustainable Fundraising

Develop and implement comprehensive fundraising strategies that strengthen annual giving, major gifts, grants, endowment support, and planned giving while diversifying philanthropic revenue and increasing long-term financial sustainability.

Elevate Alumni & Community Engagement

Deepen alumni engagement while strengthening partnerships with community leaders, businesses, foundations, and strategic partners that advance the school's mission and expand its impact throughout Hawai?i.

Strengthen Advancement Infrastructure

Enhance the school's advancement operations through effective donor stewardship, prospect management, data integrity, reporting, and fundraising systems that support long-term organizational excellence.

Advance the School's Strategic Vision

Secure philanthropic support for transformational initiatives, innovative educational programs, faculty excellence, student scholarships, and campus improvements that position St. Andrew's Schools for continued success for generations to come.

Key Areas of Leadership & Responsibility

Strategic Leadership

Develop and implement a comprehensive advancement strategy aligned with the school's mission, strategic priorities, and fundraising goals.

Partner closely with the Head of School to identify philanthropic opportunities and cultivate relationships with major donors, foundations, corporations, and community partners.

Collaborate with the Board of Trustees and Advancement Committee to establish fundraising priorities and long-term philanthropic strategies.

Develop annual advancement plans, measurable goals, and key performance indicators; regularly evaluate progress and recommend strategic adjustments.

Stay current on emerging trends and best practices in philanthropy, donor engagement, and independent school advancement.

Fundraising & Philanthropy

Lead all aspects of annual giving, major gifts, capital campaigns, endowment giving, planned giving, grants, and special fundraising initiatives.

Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward major gift prospects in partnership with the Head of School and Board leadership.

Expand and diversify the school's donor base while strengthening relationships with current supporters.

Research grant opportunities, prepare compelling proposals, and oversee grant compliance and reporting.

Develop strategies that increase donor participation, giving levels, and long-term philanthropic engagement.

Prepare annual fundraising reports that measure institutional progress and celebrate donor impact.

Donor Relations & Stewardship

Design and implement a thoughtful donor stewardship program that reflects the school's values of aloha, kuleana, service, gratitude, and generosity.

Ensure donors receive meaningful recognition, timely communication, and ongoing engagement that inspires continued investment.

Oversee donor prospect research, gift tracking, acknowledgements, recognition, stewardship reporting, and planned giving initiatives.

Collaborate with the Chief Financial Officer to ensure accurate gift recording, endowment reporting, and donor accountability.

Promote a culture of philanthropy throughout the school with the goal of achieving broad participation among trustees, faculty, staff, alumni, parents, grandparents, and friends.

Board & Volunteer Leadership

Serve as staff liaison to the Board of Trustees Advancement Committee.

Collaborate with the Head of School to prepare committee agendas, reports, meeting materials, and strategic recommendations.

Support trustees and volunteer leaders in donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.

Develop fundraising policies and donor engagement strategies for Board consideration.

Community Engagement & Special Events

Lead the planning and execution of major fundraising and community events, including the annual Queen Emma Ball and other donor cultivation activities.

Strengthen alumni engagement through reunions, networking opportunities, volunteer leadership, and lifelong connections to the school.

Represent St. Andrew's Schools throughout the community, cultivating relationships with civic leaders, businesses, foundations, and nonprofit organizations.

Secure sponsorships, auction donations, and strategic partnerships that enhance fundraising success.

Advancement Operations

Provide leadership and supervision for the Advancement Office, including staff development, budgeting, and operational planning.

Ensure the integrity and effective utilization of the advancement database, donor records, prospect management systems, and reporting tools.

Develop and monitor the Advancement Office operating budget.

Manage contracts, software platforms, consultants, and vendor relationships.

Oversee the preservation of the school's historical archives and institutional records.

Strategic Communications

Collaborate with the Marketing and Communications team to develop compelling stories that demonstrate the impact of philanthropy.

Support integrated communication strategies that strengthen donor engagement, alumni relations, and community awareness.

Partner with school leadership to celebrate student success, faculty excellence, and transformational initiatives through print, digital, and social media communications.

Other Responsibilities

Uphold the highest ethical standards consistent with the Association of Fundraising Professionals Code of Ethical Standards and the Donor Bill of Rights.

Support Parent Teacher Fellowship initiatives, including oversight of the school uniform store.

Perform other duties as assigned by the Head of School.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor's degree required.

Master's degree or advanced study in nonprofit management, philanthropy, business, communications, education, or a related field preferred.

Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) credential preferred.

Experience

Minimum of 8–10 years of progressively responsible fundraising and advancement leadership experience.

Demonstrated success securing major gifts and leading comprehensive fundraising programs, including annual, capital, endowment, and planned giving campaigns.
Experience working closely with boards, executive leaders, volunteers, and high-capacity donors.
Experience within an independent school, higher education, healthcare, or nonprofit organization is preferred. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Exceptional relationship-building, networking, and interpersonal skills.
Outstanding written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
Strategic thinker with strong analytical, organizational, and project management abilities.
Demonstrated ability to inspire generosity and cultivate meaningful donor relationships.
High degree of integrity, professionalism, discretion, and sound judgment.
Ability to manage multiple priorities while maintaining exceptional attention to detail.
Experience with donor relationship management (CRM) systems such as Raiser's Edge, DonorPerfect, Bloomerang, or similar platforms.
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office Suite, and fundraising technologies.
Ability to work collaboratively across departments while leading with initiative, optimism, accountability, and a solutions-oriented mindset.
Flexibility to attend evening and weekend meetings, donor events, and school functions as needed.

Compensation: $85,000 - $110,000

Personal Qualities

The ideal candidate is a collaborative, mission-driven leader who is energized by building authentic relationships and connecting generous individuals with opportunities to make a lasting difference. They are a compelling storyteller, an excellent listener, and an experienced fundraiser who leads with humility, integrity, gratitude, and optimism. They embrace innovation while honoring tradition and are passionate about helping St. Andrew's Schools thrive for generations to come.

Why St. Andrew's Schools?

Founded in 1867 by Queen Emma Kaleleonālani, St. Andrew's Schools is one of Hawai?i's oldest and most innovative independent schools. Rooted in our Hawaiian and Episcopal heritage, we are committed to developing students who lead with integrity, compassion, courage, and purpose.

As we begin our first year as a fully coeducational PK–12 school, we are entering a transformative period of growth and possibility. This is an extraordinary opportunity for an accomplished advancement leader to partner with an engaged Board of Trustees, dedicated faculty and staff, passionate alumni, generous donors, and an inspiring Head of School to shape the future of one of Hawai?i's most mission-driven educational institutions.

If you are energized by meaningful relationships, inspired by educational excellence, and motivated by the opportunity to make a lasting impact on future generations, we invite you to join us as we continue Queen Emma's legacy of expanding educational opportunity and empowering every learner to Kūlia i ka Nu?u—Strive for the Highest.

jobs.description:
Director of Operations Happy Home Helpers | Las Vegas, NV

Full-Time | Leadership Position

Compensation: $75,000–$90,000+ depending on experience, with performance-based upside

About Happy Home Helpers Happy Home Helpers is a fast-growing residential cleaning company serving Las Vegas. Our administrative team manages a high-volume operation involving inbound sales, customer service, scheduling, cleaner recruiting and onboarding, quality control, complaint resolution, and hundreds of moving pieces every week.
We're looking for an experienced Director of Operations
to take ownership of the day-to-day operation, lead our administrative team, improve performance, and help build a stronger, more scalable company.
This is not an administrative position. It's a leadership and operational performance role
for someone who enjoys developing people, analyzing performance, bringing structure to chaos, and continuously improving systems.
The Role You'll become the primary day-to-day leader of Happy Home Helpers and oversee the team responsible for:
Inbound sales and customer service
Scheduling and dispatching
Cleaner recruiting and onboarding
Cleaner support and accountability
Customer complaint resolution
Job preparation and documentation
Quality control
Operational follow-through

Your job isn't to personally perform every function. Your job is to ensure the people, processes, systems, and accountability are in place so each function performs at a high level.

You'll work directly with ownership on strategy, KPIs, compensation, and major initiatives while having significant autonomy over daily operations.
What You'll Own1. Lead & Develop the Team Provide the leadership, coaching, and accountability our administrative team needs to perform at a high level.
You'll lead meetings and one-on-ones, establish expectations, review performance, coach employees, address poor performance, develop top performers, identify training needs, improve communication, and create accountability for follow-through.
We want someone who can build a culture where people know what's expected and take ownership of results.
2. Sales Performance & Speed to Lead We generate a high volume of inbound calls and leads. You'll ensure we respond quickly, follow up effectively, and convert more opportunities into customers.
You'll monitor speed to lead, answer rate, missed calls, conversion by representative, average ticket, follow-up completion, and lead-source performance.
You'll review calls and outcomes, identify patterns, coach the team, and continuously improve the sales process.
3. Customer Retention Help us understand why customers stay, why they leave, and how we can increase lifetime value.

You'll track retention, churn, rebooking, complaints, re-cleans, customer satisfaction, reviews, cancellation reasons, and cleaner-related customer issues.
Rather than simply reacting to cancellations, you'll identify trends and implement systems that prevent avoidable churn.
4. Operational Performance You'll oversee the systems that make sure hundreds of cleaning appointments go smoothly.
You'll ensure cleaners are properly scheduled, jobs have accurate instructions, customers receive appropriate communication, cleaner issues are addressed, before-and-after photos are submitted, schedule changes are handled correctly, and customer requests don't fall through the cracks.
When something repeatedly goes wrong, we don't want to keep putting out the same fire. We want you to identify the root cause and fix the system that allowed it to happen.

5. Quality Control You'll develop and manage a scalable quality-control system. This does not
mean personally inspecting every cleaning.
The system may include cleaner scorecards, before-and-after photo audits, customer feedback, complaint and re-clean tracking, cleaner ratings, random quality checks, and corrective-action procedures.
The goal is to identify quality problems early and create accountability before they become customer-retention problems.
6. Cleaner Performance & Accountability You'll work with recruiting and operations to ensure we have enough reliable cleaners to meet demand while maintaining high standards.
You'll oversee cleaner recruiting, onboarding, performance, reliability, attendance, quality issues, complaints, policy compliance, corrective actions, and retention.
We want cleaners to feel supported while also maintaining clear standards and accountability.
7. Customer Escalations Our administrative team should handle most customer issues. When a situation becomes serious or difficult, you'll step in.
You'll de-escalate complaints, protect customer relationships, make sound judgment calls, coach the team, identify recurring causes of complaints, and implement processes to prevent them.
We want someone calm under pressure who can turn a frustrated customer into a retained customer whenever reasonably possible.
8. KPIs, Reporting & Data We want to manage the business based on numbers, not feelings.

You'll work with ownership to build a clear operational scorecard and determine which numbers actually matter.
Key metrics may include:
Sales:
Leads, speed to lead, answer rate, conversion, average ticket, revenue booked
Customer:
Retention, churn, rebooking, complaints, re-cleans, satisfaction
Operations:
Schedule fulfillment, cleaner call-outs, on-time performance, job-note compliance, photo compliance, operational errors
Recruiting:
Applicants, interviews, hires, activation rate, cleaner retention and capacity
You'll establish benchmarks, identify trends, diagnose problems, and turn data into action.
9. Compensation & Incentives You'll work with ownership to improve compensation and incentive plans for sales and operations.
Incentives may be tied to conversion, revenue, retention, quality, response time, productivity, cleaner recruiting, and team performance.
We want someone analytical enough to understand that poorly designed incentives can create unintended behavior—and capable of designing systems that align employee performance with company goals.
10. Process Improvement One of the most important questions you'll continually ask is:
"How can we make this operation better?"

You'll identify bottlenecks, manual work, communication breakdowns, missing procedures, weak accountability, and opportunities for automation.
We don't just want someone who solves today's problems. We want someone who builds systems that prevent tomorrow's.

What We're Looking For The ideal candidate has significant experience managing a fast-moving service operation. Residential cleaning experience is not required.

We're particularly interested in people with management experience in home services, hospitality, property management, restoration, HVAC/plumbing/electrical, multi-location service businesses, call centers, dispatch operations, or other high-volume service organizations.
You may be a great fit if you are: A strong leader.
You set expectations, develop people, and hold them accountable.
Highly analytical.
You like dashboards, numbers, trends, and figuring out why something is happening.
Operationally minded.
When you see chaos, your instinct is to create a system.
Comfortable with accountability.
You aren't afraid of difficult conversations.
Customer focused.
You understand the importance of retention and customer experience.
Calm under pressure.
Complaints, call-outs, scheduling problems, and ringing phones don't overwhelm you.
Process oriented.
You don't just solve problems—you prevent them from happening again.
Tech savvy.
You're comfortable learning CRM, communication, scheduling, phone, reporting, and automation tools.
Entrepreneurial.
You identify problems, develop solutions, and take ownership without needing every decision spelled out.
What Success Looks Like Within your first several months, we should see:
A better-managed, more accountable administrative team
Clear KPIs and reporting
Faster lead response and improved sales conversion
Better customer retention
Better cleaner accountability
Fewer recurring operational mistakes
Stronger quality control
Better complaint management
More consistent processes
Less dependence on ownership for day-to-day decisions

Ultimately, success means the company runs better because you are developing the people, studying the numbers, identifying problems, and improving the systems every day.

Growth Opportunity This is a major leadership hire, not simply another position on the administrative team. For the right person, there is significant opportunity to grow in responsibility, compensation, and leadership.
Our ownership team also operates an education and mentorship company that teaches entrepreneurs how to build and operate remote cleaning businesses. An exceptional leader may eventually have opportunities to contribute operational expertise there as well.
We're looking for someone who wants to build something, improve something, and take ownership of something
—not simply clock in and complete a list of tasks.

Director of Operations Happy Home Helpers | Las Vegas, NV

Full-Time | Leadership Position

Compensation: $75,000–$90,000+ depending on experience, with performance-based upside

About Happy Home Helpers Happy Home Helpers is a fast-growing residential cleaning company serving Las Vegas. Our administrative team manages a high-volume operation involving inbound sales, customer service, scheduling, cleaner recruiting and onboarding, quality control, complaint resolution, and hundreds of moving pieces every week.
We're looking for an experienced Director of Operations
to take ownership of the day-to-day operation, lead our administrative team, improve performance, and help build a stronger, more scalable company.
This is not an administrative position. It's a leadership and operational performance role
for someone who enjoys developing people, analyzing performance, bringing structure to chaos, and continuously improving systems.
The Role You'll become the primary day-to-day leader of Happy Home Helpers and oversee the team responsible for:
Inbound sales and customer service
Scheduling and dispatching
Cleaner recruiting and onboarding
Cleaner support and accountability
Customer complaint resolution
Job preparation and documentation
Quality control
Operational follow-through

Your job isn't to personally perform every function. Your job is to ensure the people, processes, systems, and accountability are in place so each function performs at a high level.

You'll work directly with ownership on strategy, KPIs, compensation, and major initiatives while having significant autonomy over daily operations.
What You'll Own1. Lead & Develop the Team Provide the leadership, coaching, and accountability our administrative team needs to perform at a high level.
You'll lead meetings and one-on-ones, establish expectations, review performance, coach employees, address poor performance, develop top performers, identify training needs, improve communication, and create accountability for follow-through.
We want someone who can build a culture where people know what's expected and take ownership of results.
2. Sales Performance & Speed to Lead We generate a high volume of inbound calls and leads. You'll ensure we respond quickly, follow up effectively, and convert more opportunities into customers.
You'll monitor speed to lead, answer rate, missed calls, conversion by representative, average ticket, follow-up completion, and lead-source performance.
You'll review calls and outcomes, identify patterns, coach the team, and continuously improve the sales process.
3. Customer Retention Help us understand why customers stay, why they leave, and how we can increase lifetime value.

You'll track retention, churn, rebooking, complaints, re-cleans, customer satisfaction, reviews, cancellation reasons, and cleaner-related customer issues.
Rather than simply reacting to cancellations, you'll identify trends and implement systems that prevent avoidable churn.
4. Operational Performance You'll oversee the systems that make sure hundreds of cleaning appointments go smoothly.
You'll ensure cleaners are properly scheduled, jobs have accurate instructions, customers receive appropriate communication, cleaner issues are addressed, before-and-after photos are submitted, schedule changes are handled correctly, and customer requests don't fall through the cracks.
When something repeatedly goes wrong, we don't want to keep putting out the same fire. We want you to identify the root cause and fix the system that allowed it to happen.
